MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 






We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 






Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.


To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.











Help shape the future of healthcare at Monash Health and embark on a rewarding career where your dedication makes a difference in people's lives. 






About the Department - Program 


The Monash Health Cybersecurity team helps enable safe, resilient and trusted care by protecting the digital systems, information and technologies that support clinical care and business operations. As Monash Health continues to expand its digital capability, connectivity and innovation, the Cybersecurity team plays a critical role in reducing cyber risk, strengthening organisational resilience, and supporting the safe and reliable delivery of services across the organisation.


The Cybersecurity team is responsible for protecting Monash Health's digital environment, including clinical systems, medical devices, enterprise applications, patient information, workforce technologies and supporting infrastructure. The team works in partnership with stakeholders across the Digital and Information Division and the broader organisation to identify, assess and manage cyber risk, support secure service delivery, and improve cyber maturity and technology resilience.


This includes close collaboration with teams responsible for infrastructure, networks, cloud and platform services, digital health, enterprise applications, architecture, identity and access management, service delivery, project delivery and operational support. The team also works closely with Risk Management, Emergency Management, Business Continuity, Legal, Privacy, Internal Audit, procurement and vendor management, as well as clinical, operational and corporate leaders across Monash Health.


In addition, the team maintains key relationships with the Victorian Department of Health cyber functions, sector partners, external service providers, and relevant assurance and regulatory bodies. The team also supports Monash Health's obligations under relevant cyber, privacy and critical infrastructure requirements, including the Security of Critical Infrastructure (SOCI) framework, by helping ensure cyber risks, control obligations and resilience requirements are identified, assessed and managed appropriately.







About the Role 






Join our team as a Cyber Governance, Risk and Compliance lead on a full time to work at Monash Health based at Clayton. Reporting to the Head of Cybersecurity, The Cyber Governance, Risk and Compliance Lead is responsible for leading cyber governance, risk and compliance activities across Monash Health. 






Key Result Areas:








Lead the establishment, maintenance and continuous improvement of Monash Health's cyber risk management framework, aligned with the Enterprise Risk Framework.


Provide timely, high-quality cyber governance, risk and compliance advice to stakeholders across Monash Health.


Contribute to the development and continuous improvement of Monash Health's cyber strategy, roadmap, governance and risk management capability, including the identification of capability gaps and improvement initiatives


Lead the identification, assessment, treatment and reporting of cyber risks, including appropriate governance, escalation and stakeholder engagement.


Develop, maintain and periodically review cybersecurity policies, standards, guidelines and related governance artefacts.


Lead or support cyber compliance and assurance activities against relevant internal, Victorian Government, Commonwealth and sector requirements, including the Security of Critical Infrastructure (SOCI) framework where applicable.


Lead or coordinate cyber control assessments, compliance reviews and assurance activities to evaluate control effectiveness and support risk-based decision-making.








About You 






To be successful in this healthcare role, you will bring the following demonstrated skills, experience, and attributes: 








Demonstrated experience in cyber governance, risk and compliance within a large, complex or regulated environment, preferably in healthcare, government or critical infrastructure.


Strong knowledge of cyber risk management, control assurance, compliance and third-party risk management, including the operation of governance frameworks, risk registers, control monitoring and assurance activities.


Strong working knowledge of contemporary cyber security frameworks and standards, including ISO 27001, ISO 31000, NIST Cybersecurity Framework, the Australian Government Information Security Manual (ISM) and the Essential Eight.


Sound knowledge of legislative, regulatory and policy obligations relevant to Victorian public health services, including the Privacy and Data Protection Act 2014 (Vic), Health Records Act 2001 (Vic), and the Security of Critical Infrastructure (SOCI) framework.


Demonstrated ability to think strategically and systematically, identify emerging issues, manage competing priorities and support risk-based decision-making in a complex service delivery environment.







Qualifications, registrations and licences:








Tertiary qualification in cybersecurity, information technology, risk, governance, audit, law, business or a related discipline, and-or equivalent relevant experience.


Relevant industry certification in cybersecurity, risk, audit or governance (for example CISM, CISA, CISSP, CRISC, ISO 27001 Lead Implementer-Auditor or equivalent) would be highly regarded.


Qualifications or certifications in governance, assurance, audit, privacy, business continuity, resilience or related disciplines would be advantageous.

Full-time Passive Fire Protection Equipment Technician position available with competitive salary. Work in a dynamic team in NSW.

3 Stand-out Bullet Points:
•	Full-Time Fire Protection Equipment Technician
•	Salary Range: $90,000 - $105,000 per annum plus superannuation
•	Exciting opportunity to work in a professional setting.

About Us
Essential Passive Fire Protection Services Pty Ltd is a proudly Australian-owned and operated company dedicated to delivering premier facility maintenance and safety solutions. We specialise in comprehensive fire protection services, ensuring that commercial, industrial, and residential properties remain safe, compliant, and fully operational. Our commitment to excellence, regulatory compliance, and workplace safety forms the foundation of our operations, enabling us to provide unparalleled service to our diverse client base.

About the role
The Passive Fire Protection Equipment Technician is responsible for ensuring that all passive fire containment systems are correctly installed, inspected, tested, and maintained in strict compliance with the Building Code of Australia (BCA) and applicable Australian Standards, primarily AS 1851. The role involves working with a variety of passive fire systems, including but not limited to fire-rated batts, wraps, mastic, collars, seals, fire doors, smoke doors, and fire shutters.

Duties and Responsibilities

•	Install, repair, and maintain passive fire containment systems, including fire-rated batts, wraps, mastic, collars, seals, fire/smoke doors, and shutters.
•	Ensure all installations and maintenance works are executed in accordance with manufacturer specifications, the BCA, and relevant Australian Standards.
•	Select and apply appropriate fire-stopping materials for various penetrations and construction joints.
•	Conduct routine inspections and preventative maintenance testing of passive fire protection systems in accordance with AS 1851.
•	Assess the integrity of fire compartments, fire doors, smoke doors, and fire shutters.
•	Identify, diagnose, and report on defects, non-conformances, or compromised fire separations.
•	Perform necessary rectification and repair works on non-compliant passive fire systems to restore full regulatory compliance.
•	Provide technical recommendations for the upgrade or replacement of obsolete or irreparably damaged passive fire infrastructure.
•	Accurately complete and submit service reports, logbooks, defect notices, and compliance certificates in a timely manner.
•	Maintain comprehensive digital and physical records of all inspections, tests, and rectification works using the company’s designated field service management software.
•	Capture and upload clear photographic evidence of pre- and post-rectification works.
•	Ensure the correct use, maintenance, and storage of all Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), tools, and company vehicles.

Essential Skills

•	Comprehensive understanding of the Building Code of Australia (BCA) and AS 1851 as they relate to passive fire protection.
•	Ability to read, interpret, and work from architectural drawings, engineering plans, and fire matrix schedules.
•	High level of attention to detail and precision in workmanship.
•	Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to troubleshoot complex compliance issues on-site.
•	Proficiency in using mobile technology (tablets/smartphones) and field service management software for reporting and documentation.
•	Excellent time management skills with the capacity to work autonomously and manage a daily schedule of site visits.
•	Strong verbal and written communication skills.

Qualifications needed:

•	Minimum Certificate III level or equivalent relevant work experience
•	Minimum one year of work experience on relevant position
•	White card

What We Offer

•	Competitive salary based on experience
•	Opportunities for professional growth and training
•	A supportive and dynamic work environment
•	Work on exciting projects with cutting-edge technology

Salary:  The role offers a remuneration package ranging from $90,000-$105,000 plus superannuation for a 38-hour work week.

How to Apply: 11 Recruitment is your pathway to securing this exciting opportunity. We are looking forward to facilitating your application and potentially welcoming you to a company that values expertise. Apply now and let us help you take the next step in your career.

result.description:
Our esteemed client, VK Windows and Doors, is a family-owned Australian manufacturer and supplier of premium aluminium windows and doors for residential, commercial, and architectural projects. Based in Kilmore, Victoria, the company is committed to delivering high-quality, energy-efficient, and durable products, backed by expert craftsmanship and customer-focused service. With a strong emphasis on innovation, reliability, and custom solutions, the business helps create modern, functional, and stylish spaces across Australia.

VK Windows and Doors is currently seeking a skilled Carpenter to join their growing team. The successful candidate will follow blueprints and building plans, shape or cut materials to exact measurements with hand tools or power saws, and operate, maintain, and sharpen carpentry tools. Install structures or fixtures, including windows, doors, frames, flooring, trim, and hardware, using hand and power tools. 

The annual salary for this position is $80,000 to $85,000 plus superannuation.

This position is offered on a minimum 2-year contract with the possibility of further extension.

Responsibilities include:

•	Install structures or fixtures, such as windows, doors, frames, floorings, trim, or hardware, using hand or power tools.

•	Level and help erect the build framework.

•	Utilise chisels, planes, saws, drills, and sanders to repair and erect structures.

•	Join materials with nails, screws, staples, or adhesives.

•	Examines work to make sure it meets specifications.

•	Install door handles, locks, hardware, flooring underlay, insulating material and other fixtures.

•	Follow blueprints and building plans to meet the needs of clients.

•	Shape or cut materials to specified measurements, using hand tools, machines, or power saws.

•	Operate, maintain, and sharpen carpentry tools and equipment.

•	Maintain building interiors and exteriors.

•	Prepare cost estimates for clients or employers.

•	Estimate height, width, length, and other proportions using levels, rules and framing squares.

•	Measure and mark cutting lines on materials, using a ruler, pencil, chalk, and marking gauge.

•	Select and order the material and timber for the projects and prepare the layouts.

•	Work with materials such as wood, plastic, fibreglass, or drywall.

•	Assemble prepared wood to form structures and fittings ready to be installed.	

•	Follow established safety rules and regulations and maintain a safe and clean environment.

Tools & Equipment:

•	Measuring and marking out – retractable tape measure, wind-up tape measures, scale rule, folding rule, etc.

•	Squares and bevels – try square, mitre square, sliding bevel, combination square.

•	Gauges: marking gauge, mortise gauge, cutting gauge.

•	Knives, scribes and pencils – marking knife, utility knife, scribe, Carpenter’s pencil, drawing pencil.

•	Traditional hand saws – traditional hand saws, rip saw, crosscut saw, panel saw, hard point saw, back saws, etc.

•	Hammers – claw hammer, Warrington hammer, club hammer, sledgehammer.

•	Other equipment includes – screwdrivers, planes, chisels, files, rasps, drills, clamps, levelling tools and power tools such as drills, saws, sanders, planes, routers, trimmers and nail guns etc.

Qualifications: 
 
•	Must have a minimum of one to two (1-2) years of experience in a similar setting.

•	Should have at least a Certificate III in Carpentry.

•	Ability to communicate well in spoken and written English.

Cyber Security Analyst | SOC Operations, Threat Hunting & Vulnerability Management   Your new company     Join a well-established public sector organisation dedicated to delivering critical services across Western Australia. Operating within a modern technology and security environment, the organisation is focused on strengthening its cyber security posture through proactive monitoring, threat detection, risk management, and continuous improvement initiatives.    Your new role     
 As a Cyber Security Engineer / Analyst, you will play a key role in cyber security operations, supporting the monitoring, investigation, and response to security incidents across enterprise environments. Working within a security-focused team, you will contribute to threat intelligence activities, vulnerability management, security assessments, and ongoing security improvement programs. 
 Key responsibilities include: 
 
 Monitoring and analysing security events, alerts, and incidents. 
 Performing SOC activities including incident triage, investigation, and response. 
 Conducting threat hunting and threat intelligence analysis. 
 Supporting vulnerability assessments, security reviews, and audit activities. 
 Assisting with penetration testing and security validation exercises. 
 Performing security assessments of systems, applications, and cloud environments. 
 Preparing security reports, recommendations, and technical documentation. 
 Supporting compliance with cyber security frameworks, standards, and best practices. 
 
  What you'll need to succeed     
 To be successful in this role, you will possess: 
 
 Experience in Cyber Security Operations, SOC, or Security Analyst roles. 
 Strong incident detection, investigation, and response capabilities. 
 Hands-on experience with SIEM platforms such as Microsoft Sentinel. 
 Knowledge of vulnerability management tools and security assessment practices. 
 Understanding of threat intelligence, threat hunting, and indicators of compromise (IOCs). 
 Exposure to network security technologies including firewalls, IDS/IPS, VPNs, web proxies, and endpoint security solutions. 
 Knowledge of Microsoft Azure and Microsoft 365 security services. 
 Familiarity with cyber security frameworks including ACSC Essential Eight, ISO 27001, NIST, and ISM. 
 Relevant tertiary qualifications in Cyber Security, Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related discipline. 
 Industry certifications such as Security+, CEH, SC-200, AZ-500, CISSP, or equivalent will be highly regarded. 
 
  What you'll get in return     
 
 Competitive hourly contract opportunity. 
 Opportunity to work within a mature cyber security environment. 
 Exposure to modern security technologies and enterprise-scale security operations. 
 Collaborative and supportive technical team. 
 Valuable experience contributing to critical cyber security initiatives. 
 Free onsite parking and excellent workplace facilities. 
 
  What you need to do now     
 If you're interested in this role, click ' apply now ' to forward an up-to-date copy of your CV, or call us now. 
 If this job isn't quite right for you, but you are looking for a new position, please contact us for a confidential discussion on your career.  Please  click here  to apply.
